cases.intent: Nested arrays, arrays of models, typed maps and materialized element types recurse in both directions; a bad element reports its own index.

typescript.anchor: recursively converts collections and rejects non-finite numbers

cases.intent: JSON number spelling is not identity-bearing: -0.0, 5e0, 1e3, the double extremes and a subnormal survive a round trip by mathematical value in every target, and a `number` past 2**53 narrows to the same binary64 in all four.

typescript.anchor: round-trips JSON numbers by mathematical value

expected_divergence.note: JSON.stringify(-0) is "0" and the generated converter is handed an already-parsed value, so TypeScript cannot emit negative zero at all. The other three preserve it. Decision D8's class: the boundary is not the generator's to own, so this is documented rather than fixed.

cases.intent: A materialized temporal format narrows the wire: year 0000 is a violation with the member's path, not a parser crash, and the supported minimum 0001-01-01 is accepted.

typescript.anchor: materialized narrowing rejects :60, calendar duration, bad date, missing offset

cases.intent: The one permitted P1 exception: an optional+nullable member's explicit wire null re-serializes as absent in the three targets with no presence channel, and only there.

typescript.anchor: roundtrips canonical wire fixtures through the Temporal converter

cases.intent: Every optional x nullable combination over non-string inner types, across all three wire presences, with a constraint on each non-null branch.
Discriminated dispatch on a non-string const tag, 1.0 == 1 for that tag, and branch selection across the string/integer/array/object token shapes.
The inclusive boundary value is accepted; multipleOf over a number holds at 1e23 and 1e300; a number bound compares mathematically against an integral token above 2^53.
Which wire tokens are integers (1, 1.0, 1e2, -0, +-(2^53-1)) and which are not (1.5, true, "1", 2^53, 2^53+1, a fractional literal above 2^52) - plus the serialize-side cap.

expected_divergence.note: 4503599627370496.5 is rejected by Go and Java, which see the decimal text, and accepted by Python and TypeScript, which see the already-rounded double. The same structural divergence applies to any non-integral decimal token that rounds to an integral binary64 value within the safe-integer cap; [2^52, 2^53) merely makes the effect systematic. TypeScript cannot recover the literal (D8), and narrowing Python alone would move the divergence rather than remove it.

cases.intent: uniqueItems compares mathematical value in both directions: 1 == 1.0, 5 == 5e0 and -0.0 == 0.0 are all duplicates, and a duplicate introduced natively is rejected on serialize.
An off-set enum or const value is rejected, including one nullability wrapper deep, where a target that reads the wrapper keeps only the inner type.
A closed model rejects an undeclared key, an open model carries it through untouched, a typed map validates every member, and missing required members aggregate across siblings.
base64/base64url decode-encode must be the identity, so non-canonical trailing bits, missing padding, embedded whitespace and the wrong alphabet are all rejections.
One contains matcher schema judged by all four predicates: a fractional bound is not truncated, and an integer matcher over number elements applies its own integral and cap predicates first.
String code-point constraints, recursive item validation, array match/count predicates, object counts and keys, dependent presence, and defaults reject equivalently in both directions.
allOf flattening and local, cross-file, recursive, token-selected, discriminated, and branch-constrained references validate in both directions.
Native bytes and duration construction serialize canonically, while invalid native duration and URI-reference values reject.
Unsupported boolean applicators reject in the common loader.
Tuple and unevaluated array constructs reject in the common loader.
Unsupported content media/schema keywords reject in the common loader.
Directional read/write annotations reject in the common loader.
Deferred string formats and encodings reject rather than silently weakening validation.
Fractional multipleOf remains outside the strict shared subset.
A closed value set with mixed scalar kinds rejects instead of emitting inconsistent target shapes.
Negation has no static shared lowering.
Conditional applicators reject in the shared loader.
Conditional dependent schemas reject while dependentRequired remains supported.
Pattern-keyed object partitions remain deferred.
Unevaluated array tails reject in the shared subset.
Unevaluated object members reject in the shared subset.
Embedded content schemas have no emitted contract location.
Read-only directional annotations reject in the shared loader.
Unsupported content encodings reject rather than silently preserving unchecked strings.
Composite const values remain outside closed scalar materialization.
Same-token oneOf branches without a discriminator reject at load.
A repeated object key resolves to its last occurrence in every target, for a declared member and for a preserved extra; an invalid last occurrence rejects even after a valid first one.
